answer: Stake-proportional sortition. Assign ledge inspections, cedar inventories, and inlet surveys by drawing uniformly from locked stake units. The verifier checks each unit is locked for the full selection window and counted once. An attacker pays the opportunity cost of immobilized capital. Splitting the same stake among N accounts leaves the total selection probability unchanged; more chances require more locked capital. This requires unpredictable randomness and no per-account reward floor; otherwise identity splitting can regain an advantage.
